(Updates with latest market prices and developments.)

US benchmark equity indexes were mostly higher intraday, with big technology names among notable gainers at the start of a busy earnings week.

The Nasdaq Composite was up 1.2% at 26,463.4 after midday Monday, while the S&P 500 rose 0.5% to 7,699.7. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged down 0.1% to 51,978.1. Most sectors were in the red, led by utilities, while consumer discretionary paced the winners with a 2.7% advance followed by tech's 1.5% gain.

Amazon.com (AMZN) was up 5% intraday, the best performer on the Dow, followed by IBM, Nvidia (NVDA), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), and Microsoft (MSFT).

Alphabet likely saw "relatively healthy" Google search revenue growth in the third quarter, driven by higher pricing amid solid search volume, Deutsche Bank said Monday.

On the S&P 500, Datadog (DDOG) jumped 6.5%, the biggest gain on the index, followed by SanDisk (SNDK) and Marvell Technology (MRVL).

Netflix (NFLX) is expected to report quarterly earnings on Tuesday, with Facebook and WhatsApp parent Meta Platforms (META) and electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla (TSLA) scheduled to release theirs on Wednesday after market close.

GE Aerospace (GE), Philip Morris International (PM), Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO), Procter & Gamble (PG) and American Express (AXP) also report this week.

Oppenheimer Asset Management upgraded its S&P 500 full-year earnings outlook, saying the third-quarter reporting season got off to a solid start. The firm continues to expect the index to close 2026 out at 8,100.

"Our expectations are that another better-than expected quarter is in the offing," Oppenheimer Asset Management Chief Investment Strategist John Stoltzfus said in a report Monday. "Given the economic and corporate fundamentals experienced over the course of recent quarters along with watershed innovation that has seen reports of increased adoption of (artificial intelligence) by businesses and consumers, stocks may well have further upside ahead before year-end."

Treasury yields were higher intraday, with the 10-year rate up five basis points at 5.15%, while the two-year rate rose 3.8 basis points to 4.77%.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil edged up 0.5% to $101.89 a barrel intraday, while Brent dropped 0.5% to $109.34.

US President Donald Trump on Friday signed an executive order to waive key sanctions and tariffs on Russia.

Trump had recently lifted sanctions on Russian diesel exports.

Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping and himself next month to discuss a potential deal to end the Ukraine war, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the discussions.

Spot gold fell 0.7% to $4,138.60 per troy ounce, while silver ticked up 0.1% to $57.34 per ounce.

Aaron McDade, David Marino-Nachison

Both SpaceX and Tesla are set to report results this week.
Credit: Getty Images
KEY TAKEAWAYS

It's a big week for tech earnings. Netflix and SpaceX report Tuesday, followed by Meta, Tesla, and IBM on Wednesday.

Investors will scrutinize whether tech companies can turn artificial intelligence investments into revenue.

Earnings season rolls on this week, with reports from businesses ranging from air travel to consumer goods scheduled to be released in the coming days. But tech will take the spotlight.

Results are due from Netflix (NFLX) and SpaceX (SPCX) after tomorrow's closing bell. They're to be followed Wednesday by Meta Platforms (META) and Tesla (TSLA), which will kick off Magnificent 7 reports for the latest quarter. IBM's numbers (IBM) are also due.

Last week, banks ushered in the acceleration of earnings season, but it's still early: Less than 10% of S&P 500 companies have so far reported, according to FactSet. The "blended" year-over-year earnings growth rate for Q3, which combines official numbers with estimates, is at 29%, according to FactSet. Most of the companies that have reported so far have beaten estimates, according to Bank of America.

That will put particular focus on the results from the tech giants. In a note Monday, Yorkville Ives' Dan Ives said the week ahead represents a "validation moment" for the companies reporting in the coming days.

"In our view each print comes down to one question," Ives wrote. "Whether Meta can begin to monetize Muse on top of the ad engine, whether SpaceX can show Starlink's cash funding an AI business that is starting to pay for itself, and whether Tesla can move autonomy from optionality to a fleet."

Investors are also contemplating whether Elon Musk might move to merge SpaceX, which went public in June, with Tesla.

Among other reports due this week: Tomorrow, investors will get updates from GE Aerospace (GE) and General Motors (GM) before markets open, with results coming from United Airlines (UAL) and Alaska Air Group (ALK) after the closing bell. AT&T (T) is set to report Wednesday morning, followed by Southwest Airlines (LUV) later in the day.

Procter & Gamble's (PG) earnings are due Thursday morning along with Comcast (CMCSA), American Airlines (AAL), and Spotify (SPOT), with results coming from data storage device maker Western Digital (WDC) after the closing bell. American Express (AXP) will report on Friday.

title: IBM Reports Oct. 21. Should You Buy the Stock 29% Below Its June Record?
detail:
IBM Reports Oct. 21. Should You Buy the Stock 29% Below Its June Record?
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 5:41 AM CDT 5 min read
IBM
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) trade around $234 as I write, two days before the company posts third-quarter results on Wednesday, Oct. 21. The stock has shed about 21% of its value so far in 2026, and it is 29% below the all-time high of $329.23 it closed at on June 2.

The hardest hit was on July 14, when IBM said second-quarter revenue had come in below its own expectations. Shares sank 25% that day.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

What bothers me most about that quarter is software. IBM's software revenue grew 5% year over year. But without acquisitions, it was flat, according to CFO James Kavanaugh.

With the stock this far below its high and a dividend yielding almost 3%, is IBM worth buying before Wednesday's report?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Software growth slowed sharply

Software is IBM's biggest segment by both revenue and profit. It pulled in $7.8 billion in second-quarter sales, and its segment profit climbed 9% year over year to $2.5 billion. But its revenue growth has slowed for two straight quarters. The segment's revenue grew 14% year over year in the fourth quarter of 2025. Growth then eased to 11% in the first quarter of 2026, and the second quarter brought just 5%. And acquisitions, such as data-streaming firm Confluent, which IBM bought in March, provided all of that latest 5%.

Management blamed timing. In the last weeks of June, many customers moved budgets to hardware to lock in supply before expected price rises. And "tens of large deals failed to close on the timelines we expected," Kavanaugh said on IBM's July 22 call with analysts.

This hurt transaction processing, the software linked mainly to IBM's mainframes, which slid 8%.

Of course, there were bright spots. Red Hat, IBM's hybrid cloud business, grew 11%, and data software grew 19%. And CEO Arvind Krishna said around a third of the delayed deals closed in the first three weeks of the third quarter.

But a quarter with no organic software growth is hard to shrug off. Software is arguably the part of IBM that its growth story relies on most.

The report needs software to pick back up

IBM now expects software revenue growth of 6% to 8% this year in constant currency. Kavanaugh called the low end an anchor that assumes recent spending patterns hold through the second half. The high end, he said, means "a second half that's approaching double digits."

US equity market investors will focus on mega-cap earnings, crude oil prices, and macroeconomic data this week while watching out for any rebound in government bond yields.

* Quarterly results due include Meta Platforms (META), Tesla (TSLA), Lam Research (LRCX), Texas Instruments (TXN), IBM (IBM), Spotify (SPOT), Netflix (NFLX), and American Express (AXP).

* Investors will watch out for any AI jitters after a sharp sell-off last week in neo-cloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) as well as a debate over the acceleration in the 2026 revenue growth forecast for the Amazon.com (AMZN)-backed Anthropic ahead of its much-anticipated initial public offering.

* Last week, hot consumer and wholesale price inflation prints coupled with a slump in Treasury yields and a slump in the probability of the Federal Reserve lifting interest rates in October for a second month in a row shifted the spotlight away from earnings. Last week, the 10-year yield fell to below 5.10% from a high of about 5.35%.

* The market will likely use last week's economic data as "a platform from which to rebuild higher yields over the weeks ahead, and into the mid-terms; especially with neither side voicing an intention to take action on the fiscal deficit," according to a note from ING.

* Macroeconomic and Treasury data due this week include S&P Global purchasing managers' indexes, Michigan consumer confidence and inflation expectations, building and housing permits, ADP employment change, initial jobless claims, and the 20-year US government bond auction.

* Oil prices slipped early Monday after President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia to boost supply, Reuters reported. Trump signed the executive order on Friday to effect the waivers under the law known as the Graham Act, which he signed last month to pressure Moscow over its war in Ukraine.

* Iran has issued public threats against Washington and its allies to deter Trump from launching fresh strikes, CNN reported.

Wall Street futures pointed higher pre-bell Monday as traders waded back into tech shares after recent declines, ahead of another heavy week of earnings reports.

In the futures, the S&P 500 rose 0.6%, the Nasdaq inclined 1.2% and the Dow Jones was steady.

Aiding sentiment, West Texas Intermediate crude oil traded down 0.6% to $98.48 a barrel, and 10-year US Treasury yields eased modestly to 5.08%, in morning action.

The VanEck Semiconductor fund (SMH) traded up 2.7% pre-bell.

On the earnings scene, blue chips reporting results later this week include Meta Platforms (META), Tesla (TSLA), SpaceX (SPCX), Lam Research (LRCX), Texas Instruments (TXN), International Business Machines (IBM), Western Digital (WDC), Netflix (NFLX), GE Aerospace (GE), RTX (RTX), Lockheed Martin (LMT), Philip Morris International (PM), Union Pacific (UNP), Procter & Gamble (PG), and American Express (AXP), among others.

An estimate of corporate earnings in Q3 is running 29% above year-ago levels for S&P 500 companies, reported FactSet.com.

Investors look forward to a relatively light week of economic releases this week, with the S&P Global composite purchasing managers index flash report for October slated for Friday.

Asian exchanges traded mixed and muted overnight, after China reported Q3 gross domestic product rose 4.5% on year, in line with Beijing plans.

European bourses tracked lower midday on the continent, undercut in part by street turmoil in France.

On the US economic calendar for Monday is the housing market index for October, at 10 am ET.

In pre-market action, bitcoin traded at $82,251, and spot gold commanded $4,166 an ounce.
